items.title: A mercy to the worlds
items.subtitle: The final Messenger
items.body: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ﷺ was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant. Allah chose him as the seal of the prophets—the last Messenger sent to guide all of humanity with the Quran.
items.lesson: His mission was universal: to call people to worship Allah alone and to complete the message of previous prophets.

items.title: The trustworthy character
items.subtitle: Before prophethood
items.body: Long before revelation, he was known in Makkah as Al-Amin—the Trustworthy. He cared for orphans, honored agreements, and was sought to settle disputes even by those who later opposed his message.
items.lesson: Character built on honesty and mercy prepares the heart to carry great responsibility.

items.title: First revelation
items.subtitle: Cave Hira
items.body: At forty, while meditating in Cave Hira, he received the first verses of the Quran through Angel Jibril: “Read in the name of your Lord who created.” Trembling, he returned to Khadijah (RA), who comforted and supported him.
items.lesson: Knowledge and worship begin with humility before Allah, not with pride.

items.title: Patient perseverance
items.subtitle: Early years in Makkah
items.body: For years he called his people to tawhid while facing mockery, boycott, and the loss of loved ones—including his wife Khadijah (RA) and uncle Abu Talib. He remained steadfast, forgiving, and firm upon the truth.
items.lesson: Sincerity to Allah matters more than immediate worldly victory.

items.title: Hijrah to Madinah
items.subtitle: A new community
items.body: When persecution intensified, Muslims migrated to Madinah. The Prophet ﷺ established brotherhood between the Muhajirun and Ansar, built the masjid, and laid foundations for a society rooted in faith and justice.
items.lesson: Community is built through sacrifice, brotherhood, and shared purpose.

items.title: Mercy in victory
items.subtitle: Conquest of Makkah
items.body: When Makkah was opened peacefully, those who had fought him for years expected revenge. Instead he asked, “What do you think I will do with you?” and declared, “Go, you are free”—a moment of profound mercy.
items.lesson: True strength is shown in forgiveness when power is in your hands.

items.title: Farewell message
items.subtitle: The Farewell Hajj
items.body: On the plain of Arafah he delivered his final sermon: affirming the sanctity of life and property, the rights of women, racial equality, and that no Arab is superior to a non-Arab except in taqwa.
items.lesson: Islam completes the call to justice, dignity, and accountability before Allah.

items.title: A lasting example
items.subtitle: His legacy
items.body: He returned to his Lord in Madinah, leaving the Quran and his Sunnah as guidance until the Last Day. Muslims honor him by following his character—gentleness, truthfulness, patience, and devotion to Allah.
items.lesson: Love for the Prophet ﷺ is shown by living his teachings, not merely mentioning his name.
